scope: Model/editor semantic and pedagogy review of Lesson 0135; not an independent human or real-learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: ‘How well do you remember it?’, ‘I remember it well.’ and ‘I remember the name too.’ are grammatical and natural.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: remember is consistently rendered as «به یاد داشتن» in the intended recall sense; Persian instructions and option feedback were rechecked after repair.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: Meaning recognition precedes guided dialogue; all listening, reconstruction and retrieval dependencies point backward to turns exposed in A02.

distractorQuality.evidence: All English choice distractors are grammatical, natural, semantically contrastive, and now have explicit model audits plus learner-facing option feedback.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: لیام و لیو در کتابخانه درباره زمان جلسه قبلی و یک اسم آشنا حرف می‌زنند.

difficultyFit.evidence: One A1 lexical target is combined with a controlled How + adverb question and short learner responses.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: remember recurs in meaning, dialogue, listening, selection, supported reconstruction and hidden retrieval.

transferQuality.evidence: The learner moves from remembering an earlier item to remembering a name without changing the target sense.

overallCoherence.evidence: Outcome, story and activities all focus on recalling information.

learnerExperience.evidence: Dependency ordering and source availability were audited, but no real learner test is claimed; perceived relevance and difficulty remain unverified.

runtimeAssetGrounding.evidence: No visual is claimed. A03 and A06 use audioRequired source turns only after A02 has exposed those turns; A07 retrieves T04 after the same dialogue exposure.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
Only the recall-from-memory sense of remember is assessed.
Generated audio pronunciation/prosody is not evaluated at this text stage.
Runtime behavior still requires CI validation.
